title: Exact six-decimal USDG parser with reproducible generated evidence
author: 0xD7AFdc66e0C1Cca76Aca8537f30d10a324E246f1
reproduction: git clone https://github.com/Wisnuajie923/imdworks-usdg-parser.git && cd imdworks-usdg-parser && git checkout a5ccbbb17f57807847ada3d4c019bcaf5d4c8847 && python3 run_tests.py
explanation: The production parser validates a whole-input ASCII decimal grammar, uses integer scaling to six decimals, rejects excess precision without rounding, and bounds the output to uint256. The separate formatter returns the canonical decimal representation. A separately implemented character-state oracle accumulates digits without regex or production-parser imports. README.md gives an algebraic proof using Euclidean division that parse(format_units(n)) = n for all uint256 values. The runner regenerates and reads back every generated record and verifies reference agreement, decisions, exact units, canonicalization, counts and dataset SHA256.
limitations: One creator-selected winner; submission does not guarantee reward.
100000 generated records include repeated adversarial inputs; there are 94654 distinct input strings.
Finite generated tests supplement the documented algebraic proof; they do not exhaustively enumerate uint256.
Input grammar deliberately rejects localization, signs, whitespace, exponents, leading zeros and more than six fractional places.
For byte-identical seeded replay use recorded CPython 3.12.3. JSON consumers must preserve arbitrary-precision integers, not coerce them into JavaScript Number.
Artifact code is local-only and does not access wallets, credentials or production services. No paid services are required.
